mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as accommodative policy lowers cost of capital for corporations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.0% indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases real interest rates, depressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS rises.

mechanism_narrative: In high residential sales regimes (RSAFS > 700000), rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong housing demand that precedes economic expansion and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 700000 and HOUST rises.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as supply chain pressures intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: An annualized CPIAUCSL above 5.0% signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, increasing real interest rates and depressing equity valuations for negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In low-unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 3.5%), a monthly PAYEMS growth above 0.5% indicates sustained labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals monetary tightening coinciding with economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO falls.
